title: Velocity Reward Seats in 2026
body:
Velocity Reward Seats are the seats Virgin Australia and its partners sell at fixed points prices from distance-based tables. The tables determines the points price. Domestic Business Class remains fixed by zone, starting from 15,500 Velocity Points . An East Coast to Bali Business Class seat holds at 49,500 points one-way, and each partner airline prices from its own chart. This is why the same balance buys more on one chart than another. Velocity prices its own flights and each partner airline from separate tables. The value of a balance depends on which chart the booking lands in. Here is how Velocity prices Reward Seats in 2026. We cover Virgin Australia’s strongest options, partner bookings from Australia, and redemptions that offer less value for the same number of points.
How Velocity prices Reward Seats in 2026
Velocity prices Reward Seats using distance-based tables. Virgin Australia has its own flights on one chart while each partner airline group on its own, under pricing that has applied since 21 January 2025 . Virgin Australia Domestic Economy prices vary within a range for each zone, depending on demand. Prices start from 5,900 points one-way in the shortest band, while domestic Business Class holds a fixed price per zone. Virgin Australia’s short-haul international flights have their own table, while partner airlines are split into groups. Singapore Airlines and Qatar Airways share one chart. United Airlines and Virgin Atlantic share another. All Nippon Airways, Air Canada and South African Airways share a third.
Taxes, fees, and carrier charges apply to every Reward Seat and are quoted at booking. Virgin Australia’s published ranges run from $43.33 to $342.97 one-way in Economy. In Business Class, the range is $101.28 to $335.37 as of September 2026. Singapore Airlines adds its own carrier charges in US dollars. They range from US$40 one-way in Economy to US$120 in Business Class on flights up to 4,200 miles.
The best Virgin Australia Reward Seat uses at home and nearby
The fixed-price Business Class seat provides more predictable pricing, while Economy fares vary with demand, whereas Business stays steady. The table below shows the domestic pricing per zone as of September 2026, one-way, excluding taxes, fees and carrier charges.
One-way distance Economy Reward Seat Business Reward Seat Up to 600 miles 5,900 to 12,900 points 15,500 points 601 to 1,200 miles 8,900 to 18,900 points 23,500 points 1,201 to 2,400 miles 13,500 to 26,900 points 35,500 points 2,401 to 3,600 miles 15,900 to 29,900 points 49,500 points
A Sydney to Melbourne Business Class seat costs 15,500 points, while a transcontinental Business Class seat costs 35,500 points. Short-haul international routes such as the Tasman fall on their own chart, with flights in the 1,201 to 2,400 mile band costing 17,900 points in Economy and 35,500 points in Business Class. Transcontinental and Tasman Business Class seats offer fixed pricing, which can suit travellers who book ahead. Economy pricing varies by demand, offering more flexibility across dates.
The best partner airline Reward Seats from Australia
Partner charts let you use Velocity Points for cabins and routes Virgin Australia does not operate. On the Singapore Airlines and Qatar Airways chart, Sydney to Singapore is about 3,908 flown miles. That falls in the 3,601 to 4,200 mile band. Singapore Airlines prices. the route at 29,000 points in Economy and 74,000 points in Business Class one-way. Carrier charges are added in US dollars. The same chart covers Qatar Airways. A most direct one-way journey from Australia’s East Coast to Europe via Doha falls in the 9,501 to 20,000 mile band. It costs 158,500 points in Business Class.
On the United Airlines and Virgin Atlantic chart, an East Coast Australia to Los Angeles one-way flight falls in the 7,001 to 8,500 mile band. It costs 48,000 points in Economy and 102,000 points in Business Class. On the All Nippon Airways chart, a Sydney to Tokyo one-way flight in the 4,801 to 5,800 mile band costs 82,000 points in Business Class. Velocity notes that these are minimums for the most direct routes. Itineraries with stopovers, cabin changes or multiple airlines price higher. The path flown therefore affects the points price as much as the destination.
The uses that spend Velocity Points below their value
Convenience redemptions can deliver less value for your Velocity Points. Point Hacks’ December 2025 rewards points valuation update values a Velocity Point at 1.7 cents. It adopts Australian Frequent Flyer’s quarterly valuations. Velocity’s Points + Pay feature discounts a cash fare by $15 for every 2,500 points redeemed. That exchange rate is worth checking before you redeem your points.
Warning: comparing Points + Pay with a Reward Seat is a multi-step calculation. Start by calculating the value of each point
Divide the $15 discount by the 2,500 points required. That gives you a value of 0.6 cents per point
Compare that with the 1.7-cent December 2025 benchmark. Points + Pay delivers roughly one third of that value
For your flight, check the Reward Seat price in the tables above. Then compare the same seat through Points + Pay before booking. The difference becomes significant when you redeem a larger balance
A larger balance gives you more access to more of these redemption offers, as our guide to the best uses of 150,000 Velocity Points explains. Upgrades are another option, with UpgradeMe pricing varying by route and booking class under Velocity’s published rules. Their value depends on the underlying fare. You can rebuild your balance through the top Velocity Points earning credit cards and the bank programs that transfer into Velocity .
Frequently asked questions
Do Velocity Points expire? +
Yes, without activity. Velocity Points expire 24 months after the last eligible earning or redemption activity. The details, including which activity resets the clock, are in the Velocity Points expiry guide . A balance being saved toward a long-haul Business Class booking needs occasional activity along the way.
Can Velocity Points become Singapore Airlines KrisFlyer miles? +
Yes. Velocity Points transfer to KrisFlyer at a rate of 1.55 Velocity Points per KrisFlyer mile, with a 5,000-point minimum, which opens Singapore Airlines’ own reward pricing. A 3-year expiry applies to the miles once they arrive, and this activity does not reset, though expiring miles can be extended for a fee. The conversion suits a member chasing a specific Singapore Airlines seat that Velocity’s own chart does not offer.
Do Reward Seats earn points or Status Credits? +
No. Velocity’s terms state that Reward Seats and their associated charges are not eligible for points earning, and Status Credits (the separate currency that counts towards status tiers) are not earned on Reward Seat bookings either, so a reward trip maintains the balance through its booking activity but does not grow it.
Is Qatar Airways or Singapore Airlines the better door to Europe? +
Neither wins outright, because both prices are from the same chart and the most direct one-way Business Class journey to Europe costs 158,500 points either way. The choice comes down to the flown route, the carrier charges on the ticket, and where seats exist for your dates, which is a search question rather than a table question, with the partner ecosystem guide covering how the programs interlock.
Fees, rates and figures quoted are correct at the time of publication and should be verified directly with each provider before acting on them.
